blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A crew-hours row reads 4a + 3b + 3c + 2d <= 8 over binary a, b, c and d. Which of these is a minimal cover inequality of the row?

options.text: a + d <= 1, since a and d together need 6 hours, inside the 8
options.says: A set that fits is not a cover: funding a and d is a real plan, and this row would remove it.

options.text: a + b + c <= 2, since a, b and c together need 10 hours, over the 8
options.says: Right: 10 > 8 makes it a cover, and dropping any one of the three leaves 6 or 7 hours, which fit.

options.text: a + b + c + d <= 3, since all four together need 12 hours, over the 8
options.says: It is a cover, so the row is valid, but not a minimal one: without d the set still needs 10 hours.

options.text: b + c + d <= 2, since b, c and d together need 8 hours, exactly the 8
options.says: A set that needs exactly the budget fits, so it is not a cover; the row would remove the plan b, c, d.

origin.section: A Cover Is a Set of Projects That Cannot All Be Funded

questions.stem: For the row 4a + 3b + 3c + 2d <= 8, the LP point is a = 1, b = 1, c = 1/3 and d = 0. Which minimal cover gives an inequality that this point breaks?

options.text: {a, b, c}, since its values of 1 - x add up to 2/3
options.says: Right: a cover inequality is broken exactly when the sum of 1 - x over it is below 1, and 2/3 is.

options.text: {a, b, d}, since its values of 1 - x add up to 1
options.says: A sum of exactly 1 means a + b + d = 2, which the inequality a + b + d <= 2 allows.

options.text: {a, c, d}, since its values of 1 - x add up to 5/3
options.says: A large sum means the point is far inside the inequality; only a sum below 1 breaks it.

options.text: {b, c, d}, since its values of 1 - x add up to 5/3
options.says: b, c and d need exactly 8 hours, so they are not a cover, and the sum is not below 1 either.

origin.section: Separation Finds a Cover the LP Point Breaks

questions.stem: An optimal tableau row of an all-integer model reads x2 - 0.25 s1 + 0.5 s2 = 2.75, with s1 and s2 nonbasic. Which Gomory cut does the row give?

options.says: The fractional part of -0.25 is -0.25 - floor(-0.25) = -0.25 + 1 = 0.75, not 0.25.
The right-hand side is the fractional part of 2.75, which is 0.75, not 2.75 itself.
The cut says the fractional terms reach at least f(b); at the LP point they are 0, which is what it removes.

origin.section: A Gomory Cut Comes From Any Tableau Row With a Fractional Right-Hand Side
